title: Kazakh famine (Asharshylyk)
summary: Forced collectivization, requisitioning and the forced settlement of nomadic herders in Soviet Kazakhstan caused a famine in 1930-1933 called Asharshylyk. Estimates of the dead run from about 1 million to 2.3 million Kazakhs; one scholarly account puts deaths above 1.5 million, about a quarter of the republic's population.

uncertainty.note: The Wilson Center page dates the famine 1930-1933; a 2021 regional study treats 1931-1933 as the famine years in Central Kazakhstan.
